CAP-10.why: ESEA Section 8503 imposes a strict 30-calendar-day appeal deadline and the Education Act 2002 mandates published complaint procedures, so deviation from prescribed steps becomes a reportable event rather than a justifiable exception.

CAP-11.why: Under DPA 2018/GDPR, mishandling special-category student data (health, disability, psychological-pedagogical) exposes the school to regulatory attention and reputational harm, moving error cost beyond internal correction to the 70 band.

CAP-15.why: The WA State Records Act 2000 makes unauthorised removal, destruction or transfer of government records a personal offence carrying a $10,000 penalty, creating individual legal accountability that matches the 90 band rather than mere audit-trail review.

CAP-10.why: ESEA Section 8503 imposes a strict 30-calendar-day statutory appeal window for complaint decisions, and the Education Act 2002 Part 7 requires published, mandated complaint procedures; a CSM handling education complaints must follow these to the letter, matching the 'strict compliance; deviation is a reportable event' anchor rather than the base 'defined procedures... deviation must be justified'.

CAP-14.why: GDPR Article 9 requires an additional lawful basis for processing special-category data such as health, disability or psychological-pedagogical information about students, which a CSM routinely encounters when resolving service issues; this matches the 'special-category personal data... regulated health records' anchor rather than the base 'confidential commercial or limited personal data' level.

CAP-15.why: GDPR Article 30 mandates a Record of Processing Activities across the student lifecycle, and the WA State Records Act 2000 makes unauthorised removal or destruction of government records a criminal offence with financial penalties; this creates a formal audit trail subject to regulatory inspection, well above the base 'no review' level.

evidence.regime: Education sector complaint procedures and data protection regulations

sources.title: Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA) Complaints Policy
sources.cite: An appeal of a Letter of Decision regarding an equitable services complaint governed by ESEA Section 8503 shall be filed with ED within thirty (30) calendar days after notice of the Letter of Decision.

sources.title: Education Act 2002
sources.cite: All maintained schools and maintained nursery schools must have and published procedures to deal with all complaints relating to their school and any community facilities or services that the school provides for which there are no separate statutory procedure.

sources.title: State Records Act 2000 (WA)
sources.cite: It is an offence for a government organisation employee to remove, destroy, or to have unauthorised possession or to transfer possession of government records, with penalties of $10,000.

sources.title: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act
sources.cite: Schools must take reasonable steps to have service providers that are capable of maintaining appropriate safeguards for customer information, and must require service providers by contract to implement and maintain such safeguards.

sources.title: FTC Regulations
sources.cite: Schools must take reasonable steps to have service providers capable of maintaining appropriate safeguards for customer information and require service providers by contract to implement and maintain such safeguards.

sources.title: U.S. Code
sources.cite: Schools must take reasonable steps to have service providers capable of maintaining appropriate safeguards for customer information.

sources.title: Data Protection Act 2018 (DPA 2018)
sources.cite: Schools must establish a lawful basis for processing children's data and must have explicit consent or a clear legal basis for processing special category data such as health information.

sources.title: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
sources.cite: Educational institutions must maintain a Record of Processing Activities covering all data processing activities from enrollment through cooperation with external entities.

sources.title: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
sources.cite: Processing of special categories of data such as health data, disability information, or psychological-pedagogical assessments requires an additional basis.
